children.title: Paramount Settles Trump’s 60 Minutes Lawsuit for $16 Million
children.description_short: Paramount agreed to pay $16 million to settle Trump’s lawsuit over a 60 Minutes interview; the settlement did not establish that the interview was improperly edited.
children.description_medium: On July 2, 2025, Paramount agreed to pay $16 million to settle Donald Trump’s lawsuit over a 60 Minutes interview with Kamala Harris. PBS NewsHour reported that Trump alleged the interview was edited to improve how Harris sounded, which CBS denied. Paramount said the money would go to Trump’s future presidential library and that CBS would not issue an apology. PBS also reported that Paramount was seeking merger approval from the Trump administration; concerns about a connection were reported as allegations, not proven as an exchange.
children.description_long: On July 2, 2025, Paramount agreed to pay Donald Trump $16 million to settle his lawsuit over a 60 Minutes interview with then-Vice President Kamala Harris. Trump alleged that the interview had been edited to improve how Harris sounded; CBS denied the allegation. Paramount said the payment would go to the president’s future library and that the settlement did not require an apology. The case therefore ended in a payment, not a court finding that CBS had manipulated the interview. PBS NewsHour’s report also described a separate context: Paramount was seeking administration approval for its proposed Skydance merger, and interview guest Brian Stelter said that was why the word “bribe” had come up in public discussion. Paramount and the FCC denied that suggestion. The reporting does not establish that merger review was exchanged for the settlement or that the administration conditioned approval on payment. This entry records the settlement and the attributed concern without treating coercion as a proven fact. Other incidents in the original card are handled separately.

children.title: Trump Signs Rescission Cutting About $1.1 Billion for Public Broadcasting
children.description_short: Trump signed a rescission bill that canceled about $1.1 billion allocated to the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, according to AP reporting published by PBS.
children.description_medium: On July 24, 2025, President Donald Trump signed a bill canceling about $9 billion in previously approved foreign-aid and public-broadcasting spending. The Associated Press, published by PBS NewsHour, said about $1.1 billion was allocated to the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, which finances NPR and PBS, with most of that amount distributed to more than 1,500 local stations. The bill was enacted; this report does not document later station-level effects.
children.description_long: On July 24, 2025, President Donald Trump signed a rescission bill that canceled about $9 billion in previously approved spending for public broadcasting and foreign aid. The Associated Press reported through PBS NewsHour that about $1.1 billion had been allocated to the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, which financed NPR and PBS; most of that amount was distributed to more than 1,500 local public radio and television stations. The article describes a completed federal rescission, not merely a proposed cut. It says the White House had presented the bill as a test case for additional rescission packages and reports that Democrats unanimously opposed it but could not stop it. This card is limited to the signed rescission and the reported funding channel. It does not claim that the entire $1.1 billion would have gone directly to NPR or PBS, that every local station lost the same amount, or that specific station closures followed. The original record grouped this measure with separate legal disputes, media criticism, FCC inquiries, and immigration enforcement; those actions are not part of this dated entry.

children.title: White House Media Page Labels News Outlets as “Offenders”
children.description_short: By Dec. 3, 2025, a White House webpage labeled selected outlets and reports as media “offenders,” according to Reporters Without Borders.
children.description_medium: By December 3, 2025, the White House maintained a webpage labeling selected news coverage and outlets as media “offenders.” Reporters Without Borders described sections called “Media Offender of the Week,” “Hall of Shame,” and a leaderboard; it reported that CBS News, The Boston Globe, and The Independent appeared in the first section. RSF said the page offered no factual breakdown for its accusations. This entry documents the page’s existence and reported structure without adopting its accusations or RSF’s broader evaluation as established fact.
children.description_long: A Reporters Without Borders report dated December 3, 2025, described an official White House media-bias page that labeled selected outlets and reports “offenders.” It said the “Media Offender of the Week” section then named CBS News, The Boston Globe, and The Independent, and that the site also maintained a “Hall of Shame” and a leaderboard ranking outlets it alleged had reported inaccurately. RSF said the page supplied no factual breakdown for why its accusations were correct and urged the White House to remove it. This card records the existence and structure of the government page without endorsing the page’s claims or treating RSF’s criticism as a legal finding. December 3 is the date RSF described the page, not a verified launch date. The original entry grouped this page with separate settlements, appropriations, FCC investigations, and an immigration case; those incidents require their own dated sourcing and are not inferred from the webpage.

source_fact_map.fact: RSF reported that the White House had a media-bias page labeling critical outlets as offenders without a factual breakdown.
source_fact_map.quote: Journalists and outlets critical of Trump’s measures are labelled as “offenders” with no factual breakdown of why their reporting is incorrect.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: “Misleading. Biased. Exposed.” Far from encouraging trustworthy journalism, the new media bias page on the White House website is the Trump administration’s latest effort to pillory the media. insight_facts: RSF reported that the White House had a media-bias page labeling critical outlets as offenders without a factual breakdown.
RSF reported that CBS News, The Boston Globe, and The Independent were named in the Media Offender of the Week section as of Dec. 3, 2025.

RSF reported that CBS News, The Boston Globe, and The Independent were named in the Media Offender of the Week section as of Dec. 3, 2025.

National visibility is attention, not affected population. The source establishes no direct penalties, measured audience effects, or procedural bypass.

The source does not show a direct penalty or effect on wider audiences
